Product philosophy

Our vision

Our traction

More importantly, we’ve helped over 20,000 restaurant owners, and saved them nearly $200 million in fees.

Our team

Where we work

Role Overview

The Voice AI team builds the AI that answers a restaurant's phone. When a guest calls, our agent picks up, takes a pickup order validated against the live menu, answers questions about hours and the restaurant, and sends the order straight to the kitchen, or hands the call to staff when a person is the better answer. We also build the tooling that lets restaurants go live without an engineer in every launch. If a restaurant joins Owner, our team is how its phone turns into orders and revenue instead of missed calls, and how guests get what they need while staff stay focused on service.

This is not a typical backend or ML role. Real-time voice is unforgiving: a guest on the line notices every extra half-second, every interruption handled badly, and every wrong modifier. The team works across streaming speech and LLM pipelines, telephony, turn-taking, and recovery when speech, model, or network services fail mid-call, and we measure quality on real calls, not demos. We're scaling well beyond our first live restaurants, and we automate everything we can, including with AI.

As the Engineering Manager, you'll lead this team and own its delivery and technical direction. You'll build a team that ships quickly with a high bar for quality, and you'll own hiring, coaching, career development, and performance management. Your scope spans the real-time voice experience, the systems that connect conversations to restaurant menus and ordering, and the tooling and engineering support that help restaurants launch and run reliably.

This role is 100% remote and can be based anywhere in the United States or Canada. For San Francisco-based candidates: we have a new HQ in the Presidio for optional in-person collaboration.

Why we’re looking for you

Owner helps independent restaurants grow their business. The phone is still how a huge share of restaurant orders start, and too many of those calls go unanswered or get passed to a busy host. Our voice agents answer those calls, take orders, and help guests get what they need while restaurant staff focus on service. Real restaurants are already using it, and the product has proven the idea.

The next challenge is scale. Improving call quality, making onboarding self-serve, and keeping the agent reliable across more restaurants takes dedicated engineering leadership. Today, voice delivery, technical direction, and engineering support are spread across existing leads. We're hiring an Engineering Manager to own them, grow the team, and set the bar for how we build real-time voice AI at Owner.

Our Tech Stack

 - Voice & Real-time: LiveKit, Gemini, streaming STT/LLM/TTS pipelines, full call lifecycle persisted

 - Agents & AI: Vercel AI SDK, tool calling, agent loops, conversation state

 - Backend: Node.js, TypeScript, MongoDB, PostgreSQL

 - Frontend & Tooling: React, TypeScript, restaurant onboarding and launch tooling

 - Observability & Evals: Datadog, Braintrust, LangSmith, call replay and regression testing

The impact you'll have

 - Lead, hire, and grow the Voice AI team. Give direct feedback, support career growth, manage performance, and help engineers take ownership of systems and outcomes.

 - Set technical direction and turn product goals into focused plans. Partner with Product, Design, and Customer Success to prioritize work around restaurant needs and follow through from development to rollout.

 - Improve the conversation experience: response latency, turn-taking, interruptions, and recovery when speech, model, or telephony services fail.

 - Make phone ordering dependable. Help the team handle menu options and modifiers, validate orders, prevent duplicate submissions, and hand calls off to restaurant staff when needed.

 - Establish quality measures grounded in real calls. Use call reviews, automated evaluations, and regression testing to improve order accuracy, task completion, and reliability as models and prompts change.

 - Own the team's production operations and engineering support. Build clear escalation paths, on-call practices, and incident follow-through, and turn recurring customer issues into product improvements.

 - Scale restaurant onboarding and launch tooling so more restaurants can go live with less manual engineering work.

What we’re looking for

 - Experience managing software engineers, with ownership of hiring, coaching, career development, and performance. You can build trust, rally a team around a goal, and help experienced engineers do their best work.

 - A strong software engineering background and recent hands-on work. You're comfortable setting architecture, contributing code, reviewing designs, and debugging across services.

 - Experience building and operating production voice AI or real-time conversational systems, with depth in streaming speech pipelines or speech-to-speech models, telephony, latency, turn-taking, and interruptions.

 - Experience with LLM tool calling, conversation state, and evaluations for systems whose responses vary. You can connect model behavior to whether a customer successfully completes a task.

 - Ownership of production reliability, including observability, incident response, and recovery from model, network, and downstream service failures.

 - Strong product judgment, clear communication, and a record of working closely with cross-functional partners to ship useful products in a fast-moving environment.

Compensation and benefits

 - The estimated starting base salary range for this role is $240K-$260K USD depending on level, location and experience, plus a generous pre-IPO equity package. If you feel the range is too low, still please apply and let us know! 

 - Other benefits include comprehensive health coverage, work from anywhere (remote-first workplace), unlimited PTO - plus extra fun perks!

Who we are 
 About Stripe 
 Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible. 
 Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.

 As an intern at Stripe you’ll work on projects across our stack that directly impact the way millions of businesses operate. You’ll own problems end to end with the support of your manager and teammates. It’s an opportunity to work alongside some of the most creative and technically rigorous engineers in the industry and learn how to ship high-quality work at scale. By contributing to Stripe’s codebase you’ll work across domains that give you insight into how the global economy works. Recent intern projects include expanding Stripe’s Payments Foundation Model capabilities to improve generalized anomaly detection, building more approachable fraud controls, creating safer payouts, and developing user-facing solutions that prevent costly pricing mistakes and make merchant checkout setup easier.

 The Materials practice is seeking a senior-level forensic materials consultant with laboratory experience. The company is firmly established as a recognized leader in failure/root cause analysis, corrosion damage assessment, materials testing, and consulting engineering. Our clients are typically from the commercial, industrial, manufacturing, and forensic workspaces from a wide range of industries, including performance (motorsports, aerospace, marine, automotive/transportation), industrial (power generation and utilities, pharmaceutical, petrochemical, pulp and paper). 
 This role will provide expert consulting services on matters requiring materials science and engineering knowledge and expertise for a host of clients in the industries listed above. The job includes performing root cause/failure analyses and materials characterization of a variety of materials, components, and processes, primarily polymers. 
 We produce data and analysis that are provided to our clients through verbal and written technical reports, presentations, and testimony (when required). This position has significant autonomy and is responsible for project management and technical oversight of multiple concurrent projects; reviewing and evaluating design and field engineering changes; ensuring work quality and adherence to procedures; and performing other related duties as assigned.
 Responsibilities 
 ·                     Performing assignments within the field of materials science and engineering expertise based upon a scope of work and budget prepared by the consultant and agreed upon by the client in advance of performing the work.
 Conducting or overseeing laboratory investigations: Leading and participating in laboratory examinations, including SEM-EDS, FTIR, DSC, OES, TGA, fractography, metallography, x-ray, and mechanical testing.
 Performing field investigations: Studying and determining the origin and cause of materials-related defects and/or damage.
 Gathering data for analysis from various sources and means including: test results, materials characterization, and root cause/failure analysis techniques.
 Using national and international codes and standards related to the design, fabrication, and testing of various products and materials.
 Provide legal deposition and testimony as necessary.
 Producing written technical reports of findings detailing the origin and cause of materials-related defects, corrosion, and/or damage.
 Managing multiple projects, working in conjunction with other team members (including technical/peer reviewers) to produce client reports in a timely manner.
 Building and maintaining working relationships with clients.
 Educating materials technicians, technologists, engineers, and consultants on the proper use of materials science/engineering to answer complicated, multi-disciplinary questions.
 FRENCH
 Le Groupe Matériaux est à la recherche d’un conseiller principal en expertise judiciaire des matériaux possédant une expérience en laboratoire. About RYSE
 RYSE is an innovative hardware Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) based in Toronto, specializing in connected IoT devices and smart automated solutions. We bridge the gap between custom electronics, embedded firmware, and consumer-facing software ecosystems. To help build the brains behind our next generation of smart hardware, we are seeking a passionate and problem-solving Firmware Engineer to join our team.
 The Role
 Working under the guidance and mentorship of senior engineers and the FW/Engineering Manager, you will be responsible for developing, debugging, and maintaining the embedded C code that powers our connected devices.
 While your primary focus will be on feature development and board bring-up, you will also play a critical role in product quality. You will write unit tests, develop Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) test routines, and collaborate closely with our QA/Test Engineers to ensure your code is highly testable on the production line. You will leverage modern AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate your development and documentation workflows.
 Key Responsibilities
 Firmware Development: Write, modify, and optimize robust embedded C code for resource-constrained microcontrollers (MCUs) wiht BLE and WiFi applications.
 Firmware Testing & Validation: Develop and execute unit tests, integration tests, and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test cases. Ensure all new firmware features are thoroughly validated before being handed off to the QA team.
 Hardware/Software Integration: Participate in initial board bring-up for new R&D prototypes. Intersect software and hardware by reading component datasheets and configuring peripherals (I2C, SPI, UART, ADC/DAC).
 Cross-Functional Testing Support: Work hand-in-hand with the Test Engineering Team to ensure Design for Testability (DFT). Provide them with firmware diagnostic commands and assist in troubleshooting issues found on production test fixtures.
 AI-Enhanced Workflows: Utilize AI-assisted developer tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude) to draft boilerplate code, generate unit test frameworks, optimize functions, and write clean technical documentation.
 Bug Tracking & Root-Cause Analysis: Investigate field-reported issues and QA bug tickets. Use lab equipment (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, debuggers) to trace complex timing, memory, or hardware state issues and deploy fixes.
 Qualifications & Skills
 Experience: 1–2 years of experience in embedded software development or firmware engineering (including relevant internships, co-op terms, practical lab coursework, or personal hardware projects).
 Education: Degree or Diploma in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Computer Science, or a related field.
 Programming Languages: Strong proficiency in embedded C for embedded systems. Working knowledge of Python for test scripting and automation.
 Embedded Systems Knowledge: Familiarity with microcontrollers (e.g., ARM Cortex-M, ESP32, Nordic), RTOS concepts, and basic wireless communication protocols (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth/BLE).
 Testing Mindset: Experience or strong interest in C unit testing and a solid understanding of how to test code on physical hardware.
 Lab Equipment: Hands-on familiarity with electronics bench tools (JTAG/SWD debuggers, oscilloscopes, digital multimeters, logic analyzers).
 AI-Assisted Tools: Experience using AI tools for coding, debugging, or test generation.
 Eligibility: Eligible to work in Canada.
 What We Offer
 Comprehensive Benefits: Full Health and Dental coverage.
 Time Off: Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) and company-observed holidays.
 Lab Access: Access to a fully equipped R&D lab and hands-on hardware prototyping environment.
 Mentorship & Growth: Direct, hands-on guidance from senior firmware and systems engineers to accelerate your embedded development career.

About the role 
 Marriage Reset is an online coaching company. We help married men repair their marriages, and we have grown quickly on the back of paid advertising: Meta, Google and YouTube ads that lead to a video sales letter and a booked call with our sales team. Roughly 80% of our revenue comes through that funnel.
 The paid marketing team is led by the Head of Growth and includes our direct response marketers, media buyer and video editors. They set the strategy, write the ads, manage the spend and produce the creative. We need one person to run everything underneath them, and that is this role.
 You will own the weekly numbers the team works from, the project system the work moves through, the checklist every ad passes before it goes live, the landing page and email builds, and the group of video editors who turn scripts into finished ads. Done well, the Head of Growth never has to assemble a report, fix a ClickUp board or ask whether something has shipped.
 This is a new seat. The team will grow, and the systems you build are the ones new joiners will work from. Nobody has held this role full-time before, so part of the job is working out how it should run.
 Why we are hiring 
 At the moment, the reporting, quality checks, page builds and editor coordination are spread across several people who each have other priorities. Nobody has this as their whole job, so the weekly numbers arrive late, compliance gets checked at the final review rather than before it, and builds wait behind copy. We want one full-time person to take all of that and run it properly.
 What you will be responsible for 
 Reporting. The weekly marketing dashboard and Monday report: spend, cost per call, opt-in rate, return on ad spend, win rate per writer, and the number of ads launched, reconciled across the ad platforms, Hyros, and the CRM. A monthly summary by funnel stage. If a number is wrong, you are the one who notices.
 Systems. Our ClickUp workspace for marketing: the production pipeline, statuses, dashboards, templates, and the intake from Slack. Written procedures and naming conventions for every repeatable process. An asset library organised well enough that nobody has to search Google Drive.
 Quality control. A compliance and QA checklist on every ad and email before it reaches the Head of Growth: banned words, claims, naming, landing page, tracking. A log of what launched, where, and when.
 Builds. Landing page variants and new funnel pages in GoHighLevel or ClickFunnels. Email sequences and automations in ActiveCampaign. Split-test setup. You build from the copywriter's text to the Head of Growth's brief.
 Video editors. Day-to-day management of the editor pool: the weekly meeting, the flow of briefs, turnaround and revision targets, onboarding, screening applicants and tracking the bonus scheme. The Senior Direct Response Marketer approves the creative; you keep it moving.
 Head of Growth support. Keeping every deliverable and deadline visible and on track, and flagging anything that is going to be late before it is. Booking recording sessions, running the meeting calendar, onboarding new starters, managing tool access and subscriptions.
 Automation. We use Claude, ChatGPT and similar tools every day. Anything repeatable, whether that is reporting, QA checks, drafting procedures or reconciling data, is yours to automate.
 2+ years in a marketing operations, campaign operations, or funnel-build role, ideally in an online coaching, course, or direct-response business, or an agency that serves them. 
 You have built and maintained a ClickUp workspace (or Asana, Monday or Notion) that other people relied on, and you are the person colleagues ask when they want to know how the system works.
 You have built pages in GoHighLevel or ClickFunnels and sequences in ActiveCampaign (or Klaviyo or HubSpot) 
 You notice the number that does not add up. You would rather be slightly late than send something with a mistake in it.
 You do not need managing. You have owned a recurring task, such as a weekly report or a daily check, for a year or more without missing it and without being reminded.
 You have coordinated freelancers or a small creative team to deadlines and kept them on schedule without being their manager.

 The Battery Abuse Testing Engineer owns fire, abuse, and thermal runaway testing at Moment Energy. Testing ranges from a single-cell thermal runaway to module, pack, full BESS, and multi-BESS large-scale fire testing (LSFT), run at external labs and in our own facility.
 This hands-on role plans each test, instruments the test article, travels to site, runs the test with the lab, and delivers clean data. You will report to the Certification Lead, who currently runs this work, and take on the day-to-day ownership of it.

 Coordinate with external fire testing labs: request quotes, organize test dates, arrange travel, and plan the tools and work needed on site.
 Develop test plans and instrumentation plans, including thermocouples, heaters, cameras, and data acquisition (DAQ) systems.
 Work with the Certification Lead, the NRTL lab, third-party fire professionals, and internal stakeholders to agree the exact strategy for each thermal runaway or abuse test.
 Instrument test articles: tear down battery packs and modules, install sensors and heaters, instrument full BESS units for system-level tests, and set up target units, ideally alongside a skilled technician.
 Travel to test sites, liaise with the lab, and work on site each day to prepare the test, confirm redundancy, and check that all equipment is functioning.
 Run the test, collect and save the data, and support recycling or disposal of the test sample.
 Support the build-out and use of in-house abuse testing equipment, including an ARC.

Please note: this role is with Sprout Family Health, not Tall Tree. Sprout is an independent company and a partner of Tall Tree Integrated Health, who are kindly hosting this posting. You would be engaged and paid by Sprout. The pay and terms described here are Sprout's own, and Tall Tree's employee programs and benefits don't apply to this role.
 Where: Remote, anywhere in British Columbia. Victoria preferred. 
 When: Monday to Friday, statutory holidays included. You hold the line from 6:00 am to 9:00 pm Pacific and reply within 2 hours
 Engagement: Independent contractor
 Pay: $50 an hour for active time
 Start: ASAP / Early 2027
 Be the nurse in a family's pocket
 It's 6:40 on a Tuesday morning. A dad texts: his two-year-old has had a fever since midnight, and he can't tell if this is a watch-at-home day or a come-in day. You know this family. You did their intake call and you know the big sister's name. You ask three good questions, tell him plainly what to watch for, and book a same-day visit with the Nurse Practitioner. By 7:00 he's making breakfast instead of guessing.
 That's the job. Our members call it having a nurse in their pocket. Every family who joins is told you're their guide: a nurse who gets to know them, can see their chart, and can reach the rest of their care team. We call it the Health Navigator, and we're looking for our next one.
 About Sprout
 Sprout Family Health is a family health membership in Victoria, BC, built for parents, kids and people planning a family. One team looks after the whole household: a Nurse Practitioner, a Health Navigator (Registered Nurse), a physiotherapist, an occupational therapist, a speech-language pathologist, a clinical counsellor and a parenting coach. Visits run 30 to 45 minutes. Appointments are same-day or next-day when something is pressing. Adults get a yearly assessment and Health Report Card, with goals they set with their Nurse Practitioner. Kids get well-child checks, and developmental milestone checks up to age six. 
 We think good health is more than the absence of symptoms, so we don't wait for problems. We work alongside the public system, not in place of it. What we add is time, continuity, education, and a team that knows the family. We believe people are already capable and already enough, and we talk to them that way.
 Sprout Family Health is at 555 Superior Street in Victoria, inside Tall Tree Integrated Health's James Bay clinic. 
 What you'll do
 You're the first person a family reaches, and often the one who notices something before they ask.
 Hold the Health Navigator line. Monday to Friday, 6:00 am to 9:00 pm Pacific, members text or call the nurse line, which is separate from the clinic's front desk line. You reply within 2 hours, but most often right away.
 Help families decide what a concern needs. Ask the right questions, screen for red flags, and point to the right next step: care at home, a virtual or in-person visit with our Nurse Practitioner, a virtual consult with one of our specialists, a community resource, or emergency care. When a family goes to the ER, you stay in touch and book the follow-up.
 Answer the everyday questions. What a medication is for, what's typical at this age, which local resource fits. In plain language.
 Welcome new families. Run intake review calls: read the forms, bring their history into the chart, set up preventive care reminders, and book their first visits with the team. You also have a say in whether Sprout is the right fit for a family.
 Check in before anyone has to ask. Scheduled calls with families in their first 90 days and between yearly assessments.
 Keep the team in the loop. Chart each contact in our EMR (MYLE) during your shift, hand off to the Nurse Practitioner when it's theirs, and join Clinical Rounds every other Tuesday.
 What the role doesn't do: in-person care, prescriptions or refills, or anything that stands in for emergency services. We're not a 24/7 service, and we say so to members. Naming a limit kindly is part of the job here.
 What the job is really like
 We'd rather you know this now than in week three.
 It's a tether more than a workload. At our current size, the line averages about half an hour of active time a day and stays under an hour in our busiest months. Some days are silent. But you need to be reachable and able to reply within 2 hours, from 6:00 am to 9:00 pm, every weekday, statutory holidays included. A text at 6:15 am needs a reply by 8:15, and very few arrive that early. School pickup, a run, dinner with your kids: all fine. A long flight or a day out of internet connection: not on a weekday, unless your cover is arranged.
 It's not a full-time income. It suits a nurse who wants meaningful, relational work from home around the rest of life. It doesn't fit alongside a job where you can't check your phone.
 You'll have real cover. Our other Health Navigator covers your vacations and sick days, so time off is time off.
 You work on your own, with backup. You practise to your BCCNM standards and use your own clinical judgment. Our Nurse Practitioner, or anyone on our team, is a message or a call away when you want a second opinion. Our Senior Medical Office Assistant is there for bookings and logistics.
 Sprout is a family membership. Families pay a monthly fee for care that sits alongside what MSP provides. You never sell memberships or handle billing. If that model doesn't sit right with you, this isn't your role, and no hard feelings. If you've wished you had more time to actually know the families you care for, it might be.
 You'll need 
 Practising RN registration with BCCNM, in good standing with no conditions. We verify on the public register.
 At least 3 years of nursing experience, with real time spent with children and families: paediatrics, community or public health, maternity, emergency or Telehealth.
 Confidence assessing by phone and text, and knowing when "let's get you seen today" is the answer.
 Plain language. If you can explain it to a tired parent at 9 pm, you've got it.
 Your own professional liability protection and reliable internet connection. (all communications can be done through a smartphone app) 
 A criminal record check, which we'll arrange.
 It helps if you have 
 Telephone triage experience.
 Knowledge of Greater Victoria's family and community resources.
 Experience with an EMR. MYLE EMR experience is a bonus.
 CareConnect and PharmaNet access. If not, we'll help you set them up.
 How you show up matters as much as your resume. We hire for warmth, heart, curiosity, clarity, integrity and initiative. You remember the kiddo's name. You're comfortable saying "I don't know, let me find out." You follow up before you're asked.
 This is an independent contractor engagement, paid monthly on invoice.
 $48 an hour for active time , tracked by the minute: texts, calls, charting, intake calls, check-ins, team meetings and your onboarding.
 At our current size that comes to roughly $500 to $1,500 a month. The active-time grows as our membership does.
 A Sprout family membership for your household.
 You can also count on:
 A proper start. A structured first two weeks: time and training with our CEO and Nurse Practitioner, training shifts with our current Health Navigator, and backup on your first shifts on the line.
 A team that trusts your judgment. We're small, and we want your ideas. The proactive side of this role is still being shaped, and you'd help shape it.
 Families you get to know over years , not one call at a time.
 How to apply 
 Apply through this page with your resume, and skip the cover letter. Instead, the form asks three short questions. Answer each in a few sentences, in your own words. We'd rather read something real than something polished.
 Applications come to Sprout through Tall Tree's hiring system, and we read every one ourselves. If it looks like a fit, you'll get an email inviting you to a conversation. We verify BCCNM registration before any offer.
 Sprout welcomes applicants of every background. If you need an accommodation at any stage of the process, tell us and we'll arrange it.
